The symptoms of a strain may include pain, stiffness, weakness, and muscle spasms. The affected area may also be tender to the touch or have a knot-like feeling. 

While both injuries can be painful and require similar treatments, they differ in their underlying causes and areas affected. A sprain is typically caused by a sudden twisting or bending motion that stretches or tears the ligament. A strain is usually caused by overuse, excessive stretching or repetitive motions that lead to muscle or tendon damage. 

A medical professional may be able to make a definitive diagnosis by examining the affected area and conducting tests, such as an X-ray or MRI.

However, if you experience severe pain or swelling, have difficulty moving the affected joint, or if the injury does not improve after a few days of home treatment, you should seek medical attention. A doctor can evaluate the extent of the injury and may recommend additional treatment, such as medication or physical therapy.
